decisions.reason: The citrus harvesting crate is only a narrow agricultural niche and its limited website prominence suggests weak enough market pull that, despite related plastics know-how, our learning would be better redeployed to broader packaging lines.

The foldable large container sits squarely in our core container engineering capabilities and its sustained standalone presentation indicates enough traction to justify continued refinement and commercialization.
A stackable plastic crate is highly related to our established crate portfolio, so even modest early signals can be absorbed and improved efficiently across multiple customer sectors.
The medium-duty rackable pallet builds directly on our pallet design and manufacturing base, making it a product we can iteratively improve and profitably support within the existing range.

Although technically adjacent, the spill-retention pallet appears to have lost commercial emphasis quickly and serves a more specialized use case, so its weaker learning payoff does not justify continued focus.

The plastic pallet with load retainers is a close extension of our core pallet expertise and early strong presentation suggests a practical customer need that we can continue to develop within our existing knowledge base.
